claim: A peer-reviewed Nature Communications paper published 2026-10-13 reports molten-salt electrolysis using end-of-life NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A/cm². The paper reports selective neodymium dissolution, in-situ Mg–Nd alloy formation, average current efficiency of 98.4%, and modeled LCA/techno-economic outcomes. The reported 3000 A cost is a scale scenario, not evidence that a 3000 A industrial plant was operated.

whatChanged: A primary paper and supporting data became publicly accessible 2026-10-13, reporting a potentially consequential route combining end-of-life magnet feed, a consumable solid Mg cathode, and high reported current efficiency.
whyNow: The paper supplies a fresh data/peer-review checkpoint for mass/charge-balance and process-model auditing before costly scale-up.
whatItEnables: Potential direct recovery of neodymium-bearing alloy from end-of-life NdFeB magnets.
Reproducible open mass-balance, energy, consumables, and sensitivity models for comparing recycling routes.
Targeted tests of feedstock tolerance and magnesium recovery before pilot investment.
readiness: Laboratory process demonstration with modeled LCA/TEA; independent replication and industrial operation are not established.
falsifier: Independent mass and charge balances fail on heterogeneous end-of-life magnet feed, or transparent sensitivity analysis shows Mg recovery, salt loss, electricity, separation, contamination, or capital costs erase the modeled advantage.
firstUnsupportedArrow: Laboratory electrolysis metrics plus modeled LCA/TEA → repeatable operation on variable scrap → verified 3000 A plant performance → durable cost and emissions advantage.
omissions: The 3000 A cost is a model scenario, not a demonstrated industrial plant.
No independent replication of the exact solid-Mg-cathode route was found.
Full LCA/TEA sensitivity assumptions have not been independently reimplemented.
Feedstock variability, coatings, impurities, Mg recovery, salt lifetime, corrosion, and product purity remain scale constraints.
Prior art includes rare-earth electrolysis into Mg-based cathodes and other NdFeB recycling routes; patentability/FTO are not established.
rivalHypotheses: The high current efficiency and direct alloy capture are reproducible and reduce losses versus conventional chloride electrolysis.
The advantage depends on idealized feedstock, favorable Mg recovery, salt reuse, or energy assumptions.
Existing hydrometallurgical, hydrogen-decrepitation, or other electrochemical routes may outperform for some scrap streams.
The LCA benefit is sensitive to electricity mix, heat source, and system boundaries.
crossDomainOpportunity: Open-source process model and feedstock-screening tool comparing mass balance, electricity, salt/Mg recovery, emissions, and costs; plausible analytical service, not a verified paid opening.
realWorldConstraints: High-temperature molten salts and corrosion-resistant cell materials.
Safe handling of molten Mg and alloy separation.
Continuous feed/product withdrawal, salt management, and impurity control.
Electricity/heat source, utilization, capex, and downstream purification.
